ai.definition: Carbon-fixing microbes are engineered bacteria that enhance their ability to capture and convert atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) into biodegradable polymers through genetic modifications.
ai.howItWorks: These microbes have been genetically engineered to overexpress the RuBisCO enzyme, which is crucial for CO2 fixation in photosynthesis. Additionally, their metabolic pathways are modified to increase the throughput of carbon capture and conversion into stable polymer structures, effectively sequestering CO2 from the atmosphere.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing atmospheric CO2 levels by providing a biological method for capturing and storing CO2, potentially reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating climate change impacts.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves genetic engineering of bacteria in bioreactors. This includes selecting bacterial strains, designing and inserting gene constructs, and scaling up production through fermentation processes.
ai.buildProcess: Bacterial cultures are grown in bioreactors under controlled conditions to ensure optimal growth and expression of engineered genes. The process requires precise temperature control, nutrient management, and monitoring for efficient carbon fixation and polymer synthesis.
ai.costDrivers: Costs are driven by the need for advanced genetic engineering tools, specialized equipment for bioreactor operations, and high-quality raw materials. Additionally, the scale-up from lab to industrial production can significantly impact costs.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is in an early commercial phase with limited deployment but shows potential for scaling up based on initial results.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations targeting carbon-fixing microbes. However, environmental and biosafety regulations may apply depending on the jurisdiction and scale of operations.
ai.risks: Potential risks include unintended release of genetically modified organisms into natural ecosystems, competition with natural microbial communities, and the need for robust containment measures to prevent spread.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain at this stage due to limited commercial applications. However, if successful, it could offer a sustainable solution with potential market value in carbon capture and storage technologies.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may focus on optimizing microbial strains, improving conversion efficiency, and expanding the range of polymers produced. Additionally, integration with existing industrial processes could enhance its applicability and scalability.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and bioreactor operations.

glossary.def: An enzyme involved in the first step of carbon fixation during photosynthesis.
The direct manipulation of an organism's genes using biotechnology to achieve a desired characteristic or trait.
A device used for carrying out biological processes, often in the production of pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and other products.

subsystems.name: Microbial chassis
subsystems.role: the host organism that grows quickly and tolerates industrial conditions.
parts: engineered heterotroph (e.g., E. coli) with a synthetic fixation pathway

subsystems.name: Carbon fixation pathway
subsystems.role: converts CO2 into organic carbon inside the cell.

subsystems.name: Genetic control system
subsystems.role: tunes gene expression so the pathway runs at high flux without stressing the cell.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: provides a controlled environment for the microbes to grow and fix carbon.

subsystems.name: CO2 supply and gas handling
subsystems.role: delivers concentrated CO2 to the culture, often from an industrial off-gas.

subsystems.name: Harvesting and product recovery
subsystems.role: separates the carbon-rich biomass or product from the liquid and stabilises it.
parts: processing into bioplastics, fuels, or stable carbon for storage

buildSteps.title: Select a chassis
buildSteps.detail: Choose a fast-growing cyanobacterium or engineer a well-understood heterotroph to host the fixation pathway.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the fixation enzymes
buildSteps.detail: Overexpress RuBisCO and add carbonic anhydrase to raise the CO2 concentration around it; insert all enzymes of the chosen cycle.

buildSteps.title: Rewire metabolism for high flux
buildSteps.detail: Redirect carbon away from wasteful side reactions and towards the target product, removing bottlenecks in the pathway.

buildSteps.title: Build genetic control circuits
buildSteps.detail: Add sensors and feedback loops so enzyme levels adjust to changing conditions and do not overload the cell.

buildSteps.title: Adapt to industrial conditions
buildSteps.detail: Evolve or engineer tolerance to high CO2, temperature swings, and contaminants found in flue gas.

buildSteps.title: Scale up cultivation
buildSteps.detail: Move from lab flasks to pilot photobioreactors or fermenters, optimising light, gas exchange, and mixing.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with a CO2 source
buildSteps.detail: Connect the culture to a real flue gas or direct air capture stream and test performance under continuous operation.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and process
buildSteps.detail: Separate the biomass, extract useful products, or convert the carbon into a stable form for long-term storage.

prerequisites.tech: Advanced synthetic biology for cyanobacteria and algae
prerequisites.why: genetic tools exist but are less mature than for common lab bacteria like E. coli.
natural RuBisCO is slow and promiscuous; engineered versions show improvement but not yet enough.
many photosynthetic microbes already have them, but transferring and tuning them in engineered hosts is difficult.
light delivery and gas exchange become inefficient in large vessels, raising costs.

prerequisites.tech: Downstream carbon storage or utilisation pathways
prerequisites.why: biomass burial, biochar, and bioplastic production are proven, but integration with microbial capture is still being tested.

pathway.milestone: lab strains that fix CO2 faster than wild type under controlled conditions
pathway.unlocks: proof that enzyme and pathway engineering can raise carbon throughput.

pathway.milestone: pilot-scale cultures (hundreds of litres) running on real flue gas
pathway.unlocks: data on tolerance, contamination, and continuous operation.

pathway.milestone: demonstration plants at thousands of litres, integrated with an industrial CO2 source
pathway.unlocks: credible life-cycle assessments and cost estimates for carbon capture.

pathway.milestone: large-scale deployment for carbon capture and utilisation or storage
pathway.unlocks: a biological route to remove CO2 that complements geological and direct air capture.
